A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SFT/RFT forgetting study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original fine-tuning experiments on jigsaw puzzles, math reasoning, scientific QA, and prior-knowledge retention, including Tables 1, 2, and 9 and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The jigsaw rewards, GRPO/SFT objectives, rollout filtering, periodic restarts, and self-generated-reasoning procedures are unchanged. No algorithmic or model component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions already cover COCO-derived jigsaws, multimodal retention benchmarks, ORZ math, and Sci-MCQ4 scientific QA. The math and science experiments highlighted in v4's abstract already appear in v3 Section 5.7 and Appendices F and H.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 9 retain the same base, RFT, and three SFT comparisons. The self-generated-reasoning, GRPO-recipe, and mixed-data comparisons in Tables 5–8 also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Reported dataset splits, sample sizes, model sizes, training steps, learning rates, batch sizes, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged, including the appendix experiments.

E4.justification: The learning-dynamics, perplexity, Pareto-front, output-format, learning-rate, restart, self-generated-reasoning, and data-mixture analyses are retained with the same evidence. Their increased prominence in the abstract does not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: The 16-rollout perplexity reference distributions and plotted variability are unchanged. v4 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains RFT jigsaw accuracies of 66% and 75%, and Table 9 retains 71.7% Sci-MCQ4 accuracy for SFT-Rea-GRPO-Rollout.

T1.justification: The learning-dynamics definitions, LBK formulation, Theorems 5.1–5.2, and derivations in Appendices C–D are unchanged. The definitions following Equation 5 move across a page boundary without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction broaden the headline framing from MLLMs to include text-only LLMs, foregrounding existing math and scientific-QA evidence. The abstract also qualifies the data-versus-algorithm claim with 'algorithmic differences alone'; the three principal contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: The abstract's added 'alone' qualifies its causal attribution, allowing algorithmic differences to contribute alongside data distribution. This is limited: the detailed mechanism explanations, stronger attribution in Section 6, and Appendix B limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, hyperparameters, GPU-hour costs in Table 3, preprocessing in Algorithm 1, and prompt templates are unchanged. Both reproducibility statements still promise future code release.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references retain the same cited works and relationships to Jigsaw-R1, RL's Razor, and continual-learning approaches. No substantive relationship to prior research is revised.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the title, locally revises the abstract and introduction, updates affiliations and publication headers, and adds acknowledgments. The section order, most prose, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 moves from page 10 to page 9, while the title block, spacing, and main-text pagination reflow. Figure and table content, captions, and designs remain unchanged; appendix layouts match apart from publication headers.

improvement.justification: v4's abstract more accurately summarizes the existing math and scientific-QA coverage and more cautiously attributes forgetting to data versus algorithmic differences. These provide modest gains in clarity and claim calibration. The benefit is limited because the stronger attribution in Section 6, scientific evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
